Migrating birds (철새) match the passage exactly: they fly long distances and switch between stars and landmarks. Choice 4 = migrating birds.

시계가 의존하는 사건의 특성 (1단어): 'impossible to think of a clock that does not depend on a repetitive cycle of events'. The characteristic = 'repetitive' (반복적인). This is the key word throughout the passage describing clock cycles.

③ 'exposed' is wrong: 'so this too is an iterative process, although at first exposed' — passage says 'although at first masked'. The candle's iterative nature was hidden initially, not exposed. Exposed (드러난) directly contradicts masked (가려진).

Bir Tawil 분쟁의 성격 (2단어): 'The strange result of this long-standing conflict is that...' The 2-word expression = 'long-standing conflict' (오래된 분쟁). This directly describes the nature of the Egypt-Sudan border dispute.

② 'telling' is wrong: 'you need telling us up front' — 'need' requires a to-infinitive in this construction: 'you need to tell us'. The gerund 'telling' cannot follow 'need' when the subject and the action's subject are the same person (≠ 'need telling' passive structure).

Blank: 'impossible to think of a clock that does not ____ on a repetitive cycle of events' — passage uses 'depend on'. A clock must rely on a repetitive cycle. Depend = to rely on. Reflect/impose/elaborate don't fit the meaning of relying on something.

② 'direct' is wrong: 'is known as direct functioning' — passage says 'vicarious functioning'. Vicarious = experienced through another route/pathway, not directly. 'Direct' (직접적인) is the antonym of vicarious (대리적인). The whole point is that the brain uses alternative, indirect routes.

[조건] academic, performance를 모두 사용, 정확히 2단어. 빈칸: 'feeling that your __________ is not up to par'. Passage: 'feeling that your academic performance is not up to par'. Assembly: 'academic performance' — both words used.

1899년 국경선의 특성 (1단어): 'they decided to use the conveniently straight line of the twenty-second parallel'. The 1-word descriptor = 'conveniently' (편리하게). This describes why Britain chose this particular line — it was conveniently straight.

④ 'can recognizing' is wrong: 'the brain can recognizing a face by the shape of the eyes' — after the modal verb 'can', the bare infinitive is required: 'can recognize'. 'Recognizing' (present participle) cannot follow a modal verb.

④ 'is' is wrong: 'It seems to yield a smooth time scale but in fact is not' — the verb must parallel 'yield' (from 'seems to yield'): 'but in fact does not' (does not yield). 'Is not' breaks the verb parallelism; 'does not' is the correct auxiliary to echo the main verb 'yield'.
